hook: One weekend detox won't fix a two-year calibration. But it's not supposed to.
topic: The reset vs. the maintenance model — what a detox is actually for
body:
**One weekend detox won't fix a two-year calibration. But that's not what it's for.**

If you go into a dopamine reset expecting a permanent cure, you'll be disappointed. The threshold will drift back. The inputs will find their way in. Habits are pressure that accumulates over time, and pressure reasserts itself.

A reset is not the solution. It's a recalibration point — a return to a baseline from which new architecture can be built. Its job is to drop the threshold far enough that you can function differently for long enough to install something more durable.

The mistake is treating the detox as the destination. The destination is a maintained operational environment — a set of defaults, habits, and design choices that keep the stimulus load at a level compatible with the work you want to do. The detox creates the conditions for that to be built. It doesn't build it.

This is why the protocol includes a reintroduction phase and a maintenance model. Because the inputs aren't going away permanently. The question is what relationship you build with them when you bring them back.

The full model is in the link in bio.
